page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.8xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs combined with 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated hardware graphics acceleration, operating with zero GPUs.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps to handle cross-service communication and external data flow. The configuration does not feature complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not provide bundled local NVMe storage. Consequently, persistence and primary storage workloads require attachment to network-based block storage infrastructure.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory configuration alongside dedicated 3.4 GHz processor frequencies, the ecs.hfr9i.8xlarge is engineered for demanding memory-bound applications that concurrently benefit from elevated clock speeds. Tradeoffs include complete reliance on external block devices for storage IOPS and lack of onboard accelerators. The resource profile aligns well with in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational database engines, electronic design automation (EDA), and distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.8xlarge is a memory-dense, high clock speed server instance based on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at a nominal 3.4 GHz, the configuration supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, equating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance provides 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes zero dedicated GPUs. Local storage is not provided, making persistent storage dependent entirely on external network volumes. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Due to its balanced combination of high core frequency and generous memory allocation, the ecs.hfr9i.8xlarge is structurally fitted for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory databases, electronic design automation tooling, and data analytics pipelines that require reliable multi-core throughput alongside high memory density.
